newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA BANKS RAISE $700MLN OFFSHORE IN LAST MONTH.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA BANKS RAISE $700MLN OFFSHORE IN LAST MONTH.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa became the fourth bank in as many weeks to raise an offshore loan on Friday, bringing the total amount of loans raised to nearly $700 million since early February.
Absa said it had raised a $160 million offshore loan which it would use for general corporate purposes.

It has been preceded by First National Bank , which announced on February 11 that it had secured a $250 million loan, followed by Stanbic , which announced on February 18 that it had raised a $130 million loan.
They in turn were followed by NBS and Standard London, who announced last Friday that they had raised $70 and $80 million rand loans respectively.
Analysts said the spate of offshore loans in recent weeks reflected a desire by banks to diversify their funding bases.

The continuing liquidity squeeze on the domestic money market, where the shortage has hovered around the 10 billion rand mark for the last two months, was also cited as a possible motive for borrowing offshore.
"It is not extremely attractive funding, it's probably a bit more expensive than local funding," UAL Merchant Bank Treasury general manager Peter Lane said.

"But I think the banks take the view that if they did not borrow offshore there would be a lot more upward pressure on domestic funding rates and the whole cost of funding could move up," Lane said. "It could be a way of alleviating the money market shortage."
Doug Anderson, managing executive of Absa Treasury and international bank, said the rationale behind its decision to raise money offshore was based on cost differentials.
"If we raise money, we are raising it primarily because there is an advantage from a cost point of view of on-lending to clients or using it ourselves," Anderson said.
